chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When does the charity (Zakat) become obligatory upon the lamb?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is a year old (has its teeth cut/grown).'

key_terms.أَجْذَعَ: A technical term indicating the animal has reached a specific age/maturity, often referring to the cutting of teeth (typically one year old for sheep).
key_terms.السَّخْلُ: A young sheep or goat, specifically a lamb.
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: Zakat (alms-tax/charity) in the context of livestock.

ai.seo_question: When does Zakat become obligatory on a lamb according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise biological marker for Zakat liability on livestock, defining 'ajdha' as the stage where the animal's teeth have emerged, typically signifying one year of age. This specific criterion ensures that the obligation is triggered only when the animal has reached a stable, mature state suitable for wealth accumulation, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on tangible physical maturity in determining financial duties.
